title: helm(private): values templating + upgrade/rollback hook improvements for Private chart
author: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Improve Helm chart templating and add robust upgrade/rollback hooks for redwood-private to reduce failure modes during in-place upgrades and rollbacks. This change adds schema-aware templating for values.v3 -> values.v4 migrations, validates encryption/nodeselector/tolerations before applying in-cluster changes, and hardens initJobs so they are idempotent and safe to re-run on rollback.

Motivation: We continue to see upgrade incidents where optional fields (tolerations, nodeSelector, kms config) cause template rendering differences across clusters and cause Helm to mark upgrades as failed or leave dangling initJobs. This PR centralizes schema-aware defaults, makes migration jobs conditional, and adds a pre-upgrade validate hook + an on-fail rollback cleanup job to reduce manual intervention.

What changed:
- templates/init-jobs.yaml: introduce idempotent init jobs for postgres backups and kms key checks; jobs are gated by .Values.initJobs.enable and annotated with helm.sh/hook-weight to ensure ordering.
- templates/hooks/validate-schema-job.yaml: pre-upgrade Job that runs a small validator (kubeval + custom checks) against rendered values; fails fast to prevent bad upgrades.
- templates/hooks/rollback-cleanup-job.yaml: job that runs only on upgrade failure or when helm rollback is invoked; cleans partial CRs and temporary PV attachments.
- templates/_helpers.tpl: new helper functions for safeMerge, defaultTolerations, and nodeSelectorTemplate to reduce duplication and ensure stable rendering between chart versions.
- values.schema.json: extended schema (v4) to include kms.enabled, tolerations (array), nodeSelector (map), initJobs.enable flags, and migration.version.
- values.yaml: add recommended defaults and migration notes for operators.
- Chart.yaml: bump chart version to 2.4.0 and added appVersion note for private-installer.
- tests/helm: added unit tests for template rendering and a smoke test that simulates a rollback path.
- docs/upgrade.md: documented the v3->v4 migration flow and safe rollback procedures.

Checklist: 
- [x] Add schema changes and tests
- [x] Add pre-upgrade validation hook
- [x] Add rollback cleanup job
- [x] Update docs and release notes
- [x] CI green after one rerun

Notes on behavior:
- All new jobs are opt-in via .Values.initJobs.enable (default true for supported platforms); they are annotated with helm.sh/hook: pre-upgrade/post-upgrade/post-rollback depending on purpose.
- Migration path: when migration.version is present and less than current, chart will render a migration Job which performs non-destructive checks and writes a migration annotation. The migration Job uses a ConfigMap-based semaphore so re-runs are safe.
- Rollback safety: the rollback-cleanup-job removes the migration annotation and attempts to revert optional field changes (tolerations/nodeSelector) applied by chart helpers. It will not delete user-managed resources.

Backward compatibility: The template helpers default to previous semantics when values are omitted so existing users should see no change when upgrading. However, operators with custom value shapes that relied on undocumented templates should validate with the pre-upgrade hook.

Follow-ups:
- ENG-3502: Add e2e upgrade testing in perf-canary pipeline for private clusters.
- ENG-3510: Add stronger RBAC for migration/cleanup jobs (separate PR).
